currentContext.expansion: STUDDS operates four active manufacturing facilities in Faridabad, Haryana, with a fifth facility under construction. Facility V is the next stage of scale: it is expected to take installed capacity from approximately 9.5 million units to 12.5 million units through two phases, and the commencement of commercial production is now expected before the end of Q2 of FY 2027. The expansion is designed with flexibility, allowing allocation between STUDDS and SMK as demand patterns change across mass, mid-market and premium segments. The Company incurred capex of Rs.480 million during FY2025-26, and states planned capex of approximately Rs.1,600 million for the Facility V expansion, positioned to support future growth across brands, markets and product categories. The existing platform is vertically integrated across the helmet value chain — EPS liner production, in-house mould-making and 3D printing, shell fabrication, robotic and automated painting lines, hard coating, metallizing, water decal application, fabric stitching, conveyorised assembly, testing and dispatch — supported by a VCA-certified in-house element testing laboratory and an electronics lab established in 2021 for smart-helmet and bluetooth development. In FY2025-26 the Company produced 8.27 million helmets and boxes, with capacity utilisation of 89% for helmets and boxes, 88% for EPS and 57% for water decals. Internationally, the Company is expanding US reach through its wholly owned subsidiary Bikerz US Inc.

risks.risk: Regulatory risk — stringent safety standards and certification regimes, now compounded by post-listing securities and disclosure obligations
risks.note: The Company operates in a highly regulated industry subject to stringent safety standards and certifications; non-compliance could lead to penalties, product recalls, operational halts and reputational damage. Post-listing it must also comply with securities laws, listing regulations and enhanced disclosure requirements. Mitigation is continued investment in testing facilities and technologies, rigorous quality control through the production cycle, internal controls, periodic compliance reviews and professional advisors

risks.risk: Competition risk — a large unorganised segment alongside established brands
risks.note: The presence of a large unorganised segment and competition from established brands creates pricing pressure, limits market share expansion opportunities and poses scalability challenges. Mitigation is advancing manufacturing technology to raise quality while reducing cost, backward integration for better control over critical component supply, and automation of key processes including material handling

risks.risk: Market risk — failure to keep pace with evolving customer preferences on style, design, safety features and innovation
risks.note: Failure to understand and respond to changing preferences could lead to declining demand and erosion of market share. Mitigation is continuous staff training, regular market research and customer feedback mechanisms, and investment in design and R&D so the portfolio remains contemporary

risks.risk: Supply chain risk — dependence on a limited supplier base
risks.note: Over-dependence on a limited supplier base and supply-chain vulnerabilities could lead to production delays, increased costs and inability to meet customer demand during peak seasons or market opportunities. Mitigation is supplier diversification and local sourcing, backward integration in EPS and in-house mould-making, decals, painting, testing and assembly, strategic inventory planning and supplier relationship programmes; the Company states sourcing remains stable and material availability is not a concern but continues to monitor input markets

risks.risk: Financial risk — raw material price volatility in petroleum-based inputs
risks.note: The Company remains exposed to fluctuations in key raw material prices, particularly petroleum-based inputs such as ABS plastic and polycarbonate; significant fluctuations could adversely impact profitability margins and overall financial performance. During the year the Company witnessed an increase in certain raw material prices and is evaluating measures including procurement efficiency, operating improvements, cost optimisation, product mix management and calibrated pricing actions, with manufacturing efficiency, premiumisation and backward integration as an additional buffer

risks.risk: Geopolitical and trade disruption affecting freight, input costs and export markets
risks.note: The MD&A flags tariff adjustments, regional conflicts and supply-chain disruptions as watchpoints for businesses with exposure to global raw material, logistics and export markets; tensions in West Asia affected shipping routes, energy logistics and commodity markets during the year, contributing to freight volatility, input-cost pressure and uncertainty in availability of critical materials and services

risks.risk: Reliance on an outsourced internal audit model for assurance
risks.note: Internal audit is delivered through an outsourced model with reviews performed by Deloitte, an independent audit firm, with scope approved by the Audit Committee and Board; assurance over risk management, control and governance processes therefore depends on that external arrangement and on Audit Committee oversight of findings and remediation

themes.title: Auto OEM cycle - CV replacement & PV premiumization
themes.need: GST 2.0 rate rationalization plus an aged CV fleet still frames the replacement cycle, but Q1FY27's real signal is 2W OEMs EXPANDING margin through a commodity shock. TVSMOTOR sold 1.63mn units (+28%) on INR 13,896cr revenue (+38%) while lifting EBITDA margin 30bps to 12.8% having absorbed a ~4% commodity shock with only ~1.5% of price increase (CARE upgraded it AA+ to AAA), and committed 2W capacity from 6.8mn to 8.3mn by Q4FY27. BAJAJ-AUTO set volume/revenue/EBITDA records with margin at 20.9% (+110bps) through ~4.5% commodity inflation AND ~10% of volume lost to a ransomware shutdown, with EV now 30% of domestic revenue at double-digit EBITDA and Chetak EBITDA-positive - a scaled, profitable EV second engine. Commercial mobility is electrifying fastest: TVSMOTOR's 3W EV penetration crossed 40% for the first time. ASHOKLEY's all-time-high CV volumes (220k units, MHCV share 30.8%) carry the CV leg with defence + Switch EV optionality; TMCV/TMPV/SMLMAH/ESCORTS on CV/tractors; APOLLOTYRE/JKTYRE/BALKRISIND/MRF on tyres.
themes.driver: Capacity commissioning against demand (TVSMOTOR 2W to 8.3mn by Q4FY27, BAJAJ-AUTO 7m to 9m+ units); 3W/2W EV penetration inflection; GST-2.0 price-cut demand, aged-fleet replacement and festive 2W/PV.

guidance.body: Stable outlook, expected to maintain dominant market position

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Helmet manufacturers in India are experiencing a trend towards consolidation, driven by regulatory change (pillion-rider mandate, mandatory helmet change at the time of two-wheeler purchase, more stringent safety standards), rising consumer awareness of road safety, and a replacement/fashion-driven market shifting towards premiumisation
- Export revenue rose to ~20% of total revenue in FY2025-26 from 16.75% in FY2024-25, with SMK contributing ~15% of revenue — an increasingly important part of the growth mix
- SMK's premium mix acts as the margin lever, with its margin profile running above STUDDS
- Indian two-wheeler industry recovery, with retail sales up 10.70% year-on-year to 2.17 crore units in FY2025-26 and the e2W segment growing 21.81%, plus a shift in preference towards scooters and executive motorcycles signalling deepening premiumisation
- Policy tailwinds during the year: GST 2.0 rationalisation moving motorcycles up to 350cc from the 28% slab to 18%, income-tax relief, repo-rate reductions, PM E-DRIVE and the PLI-Auto scheme — together improving affordability and showroom conversion, particularly in H2
- Indian macro backdrop: GDP growth estimated at 7.4% for FY 2025-26 and projected at 6.8-7.2% for FY 2026-27, with inflation at a historic low supporting domestic purchasing power
- Global backdrop remains stable but uneven — tariff adjustments, regional conflicts and supply-chain disruptions are flagged as watchpoints for businesses with exposure to global raw material, logistics and export markets
- Manufacturing utilisation headroom — helmets and boxes at 89%, EPS at 88% and water decals at 57% — points to high utilisation in core assembly while leaving selective room in linked capabilities

capital_allocation.body: efficient working capital management, strong liquidity

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: STUDDS operates four active manufacturing facilities in Faridabad, Haryana, with a fifth facility under construction. Facility V is the next stage of scale: it is expected to take installed capacity from approximately 9.5 million units to 12.5 million units through two phases, and the commencement of commercial production is now expected before the end of Q2 of FY 2027. The expansion is designed with flexibility, allowing allocation between STUDDS and SMK as demand patterns change across mass, mid-market and premium segments. The Company incurred capex of Rs.480 million during FY2025-26, and states planned capex of approximately Rs.1,600 million for the Facility V expansion, positioned to support future growth across brands, markets and product categories. The existing platform is vertically integrated across the helmet value chain — EPS liner production, in-house mould-making and 3D printing, shell fabrication, robotic and automated painting lines, hard coating, metallizing, water decal application, fabric stitching, conveyorised assembly, testing and dispatch — supported by a VCA-certified in-house element testing laboratory and an electronics lab established in 2021 for smart-helmet and bluetooth development. In FY2025-26 the Company produced 8.27 million helmets and boxes, with capacity utilisation of 89% for helmets and boxes, 88% for EPS and 57% for water decals. Internationally, the Company is expanding US reach through its wholly owned subsidiary Bikerz US Inc.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Market leadership — 27.3% share by volume and 25.5% by value in the domestic market as of Fiscal 2024, and the world's largest two-wheeler helmet manufacturer by volume in Calendar Year 2024 (CARE Report)
- Vertical integration across critical processes (EPS liners, mould-making, shell fabrication, painting, hard coating, metallising, decals, stitching, assembly, testing), supporting quality control, cost efficiency, product consistency and faster execution
- Manufacturing flexibility — production can be calibrated across STUDDS, SMK and private-label requirements depending on demand visibility and product mix
- Dual-brand architecture spanning mass/mid-market (STUDDS) and premium (SMK), with SMK EBITDA margin running approximately 10 percentage points above STUDDS
- Distribution depth — pan-India network of around 360+ active distributors plus EBOs, alongside brand recall built over nearly five decades
- Export presence across more than 70 countries with manufacturing scale and certifications supporting international participation
- Wholly owned US subsidiary Bikerz US Inc. delivered its first year of profitability in FY2025-26, and a newly incorporated Italy subsidiary in Reggio Emilia is designed as a direct-to-dealer hub for Europe

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Capacity creation through Facility V — installed capacity of approximately 9.5 million units is being expanded to 12.5 million units through two phases, built with flexibility to allocate output between STUDDS and SMK as demand patterns change across mass, mid-market and premium segments
- Premiumisation led by SMK, which has moved from a premium label into a growth engine with a three-year volume CAGR of ~52%, ASP of ~Rs. 2,550 and a margin profile above STUDDS
- Shift exports from shipment-led presence to structured market-building, with the US and Europe central to the plan
- Direct dealer …

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [Customer] Strategic engagement with Decathlon is "progressing well", which management says provides an opportunity to further strengthen presence in the organised and institutional segment.
- [Acquisition] Bikerz US Inc. was acquired (shown at 2024 on the journey timeline) to strengthen the distribution network in the USA; the deck's board bio separately notes the entity was incorporated in 2021 by director Pankaj Duhan.
- [Industry/Regulation] BIS mandate enforcement is cited as removing unorganised/low-quality supply and boosting organised players, alongside tighter global norms (ECE 22.06 / DOT / JIS). CareEdge Research data in the deck shows the Indian helmet market at INR 13,650 Mn (FY19), 20,800 Mn (FY24) and 31,500 Mn (FY29) with units of 21, 26 and 35 Mn, and India helmet penetration of ~0.6 per biker versus global ~1.5.
- [Guidance] Management guides EBITDA margin to ~14-15% in Q2FY27E and ~18-20% in Q4FY27E on a run-rate basis, subject to stable commodity prices.
- [Brand] SMK participated in the Moto4 Latin America Cup, hosted as part of the MotoGP World Championship in Goiania, Brazil, positioned as a route to global brand equity and accelerated penetration in Latin America.
